holidays.name: National Bavarian Crepes Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the Bavarian crepe, a delicate pancake-like treat traditionally filled with a sweet cream and topped with fruit or chocolate. Grab a spatula and flip your way to dessert bliss!
holidays.origin: One of many food-themed days popularized by American food-holiday calendars. Bavarian crepes are linked to German-style desserts that combine thin French-style crepes with Bavarian cream filling.
holidays.funFact: Bavarian cream, the classic filling, is thickened with gelatin and whipped cream, and it dates back to the 19th century when famed French chef Marie-Antoine Carême refined it.

holidays.name: National Goof Off Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to skipping the to-do list and goofing off. Hide the spreadsheets, blow bubbles, build a blanket fort, and unapologetically waste time in the name of fun.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that has been popular on fun-holiday calendars, encouraging people to take a break from responsibilities and embrace playfulness.
holidays.funFact: Research on play and creativity suggests that short breaks for unstructured fun can boost problem-solving and productivity afterward, so goofing off may be a legit work strategy.

holidays.name: World Water Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that raises awareness about the global water crisis and the billions of people living without access to safe water. It is less wacky than other holidays, but it is a great excuse to appreciate your tap and take a very pointed look at your leaky faucet.
holidays.origin: Recommended at the 1992 UN Conference on Environment and Development in Rio de Janeiro, and first observed in 1993. Each year has a different theme.
holidays.funFact: Your body is roughly 60 percent water, which means you are basically a walking, talking, slightly sarcastic water balloon.

holidays.name: As Young As You Feel Day
holidays.description: A day to ignore the number on your birth certificate and act like the age you feel inside. Whether that is 8 or 108, you are encouraged to dance in the kitchen, ride a bike, or demand a juice box.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that encourages people to embrace a youthful attitude, tied to the old saying that you are only as old as you feel.
holidays.funFact: Studies on subjective age have found that people who feel younger than their actual age often report better health and well-being later in life.

holidays.name: National Chia Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the humble chia seed, from healthy pudding to the fuzzy green sprouts of a certain famous terracotta pet. Sprinkle some on your yogurt or finally grow that green-haired ceramic critter.
holidays.origin: A modern food and pop culture observance celebrating chia seeds, which were a staple of ancient Aztec and Mayan diets, and the novelty Chia Pet that began airing its jingle in the 1980s.
holidays.funFact: The word chia is related to the Mayan word for strength, and Aztec runners reportedly relied on the seeds for energy on long journeys.
